as made on 26 May 2034

# Quayside Byelaws (legal archive)

* `byelaws/original.txt`: the byelaws as first made.
* `orders/`: amendment orders (AO-n) and correction notices (CN-n), numbered in the order they were made.
* `drafts/`: consultation drafts. They were never made and have no legal effect.
* `notices/`: general notices, not part of the law.

Rules for reading the orders: an order's changes apply from its commencement date, or from the date a paragraph
gives for itself. The figure in force on a day is the one set by the latest-commencing change before or on that day
(the higher-numbered order wins if two commence together). "For the figure X substitute Y" refers to the figure
in the law at the time. A correction notice works as if the order had been printed correctly. An order that was
revoked before it commenced is treated as never made.

Pennywhistle Community Clinic
QUAYSIDE BYELAWS
as made on 22 February 2034

1. Waste oil. Waste oil must be handed to the reception tank within 16 hours of arrival.

2. Maximum vessel length. No vessel longer than 30 metres may berth at the north quay.

3. Late departure surcharge. A surcharge of 54 credits applies to any vessel departing after its booked time.

4. Fuel jetty. No more than 4 vessels may use the fuel jetty at one time.

5. Mooring limit. A vessel may remain at a visitor berth for no more than 41 consecutive hours.

6. Berthing fee. The fee for a visitor berth is 73 credits per night.

7. Pump-out. A vessel with a holding tank must use the pump-out station at least once every 10 days in port.

8. Speed limit. Inside the harbour limits no vessel shall exceed 7 knots.
